title: The Saltworks Ratio
story: In the sun-white saltworks of Pale Harbor, Corvanthe the Brine Steward has locked the drying pans and demands a perfect curing paste before she will free the salt-rakers. The paste must mix grey salt and powdered kelp in a ratio of 5 to 3, and Corvanthe wants exactly 96 pounds of paste. Mr 6 ties on an apron, dusts off his helmet, and picks up the scoop.
question: How many pounds of grey salt go into the 96 pounds of paste?
solution: The ratio 5 to 3 makes 5 + 3 = 8 equal shares.
Grey salt is 5 shares: 5 x 12 = 60 pounds.
praise: Splitting the mix into equal shares was exactly the right move — the last step was multiplying by the 5 salt shares.
hint: Add the two ratio numbers first to see how many equal shares the 96 pounds must be cut into.
victory: Corvanthe tastes the paste, blinks, and declares it 'distressingly perfect.' She unlocks the drying pans and hires Mr 6 as honorary Scoop Knight.
imagePrompt: A tall heron-like brine steward in salt-crusted robes looming over glittering white drying pans at noon, while a small knightly number 6 calmly measures grey salt into a wooden tub.
